## TL;DR

Review round 3 of the command palette QA pass. The latest checkpoint before this
round already had the review's main fix: `closeOverlay` checks the caller's
trigger with `isConnected` and falls back to the remembered element, then to the
header pill. This round I confirmed that fix against the review's scenario,
removed a stale comment that described a parameter that no longer exists, and
added a regression test for the doc-result path the review named. The palette
test file passes (23 tests). The scoped `repoos check` result is in the handoff
status, not here.

## Work and rationale

- **Detached caller trigger (the review's bug).** A context-scope doc or skill
  result calls `router.push` before the focus timeout runs. That push can unmount
  `ContextView`, which removes `contextSearchBtn`. `closeOverlay` now resolves the
  target inside the `setTimeout(0)` callback. It uses the caller only when
  `isConnected` is true. Otherwise, for dismissals and in-place results
  (`restoreFocus` true), it uses `rememberedFocus()`, which falls back to the
  header `.search-input` pill. Task results pass `restoreFocus` false because the
  drawer takes focus, so a detached caller there correctly leaves focus alone.
- **Regression test.** The existing "trigger was unmounted" test dismisses with
  Escape, and the mocked router never unmounts anything. The new test opens a
  context-scope doc result with a detached caller (Enter on the highlighted
  row) and asserts focus lands on the pill. I did not run it against the
  pre-fix code, so I have not shown it fails without the change.
- **Stale comment.** The JSDoc above `rememberedFocus` still described a
  `fallbackFocus` parameter that was removed. Two comment blocks sat above one
  function, and one described behaviour that no longer exists. I deleted the stale
  block and left the accurate one.
- **Task-result edge case: not a bug.** The review asked what happens if
  `ui.openTask` fails. I read `openTask` in `src/ui-app/src/stores/ui.ts`. It calls
  `open(t)` synchronously, so the drawer opens, and its one network call is
  wrapped in a `catch` that keeps the local task. It cannot reject, so the
  focus-on-body concern does not arise. I left the code unchanged. The previous
  draft's claim that a failed open was handled was wrong, and I replaced it.
- **Load race (other branch).** The in-flight counter from the checkpoint means
  the loading flag clears only when every fetch settles. The new test "keeps the
  loading state until the older load settles" covers the case where the newer
  load finishes first. It passes.
- **Remembered `body`.** When nothing was focused on open, `lastFocused` is
  `body`, and `rememberedFocus` treats that as no target, so the pill fallback
  runs. The existing "nothing was focused before opening" test covers it.

## Approaches tried

- Resolving the caller at call time would have been simpler. I rejected it,
  because `router.push` is started before the timeout and the trigger might
  still be connected at call time and detached a moment later. Resolving inside
  the timeout checks the state that matters for focus.
- I considered a separate focus path for doc results. A single fallback chain in
  `closeOverlay` covers Escape, the ✕ button, backdrop clicks and in-place results
  with one rule, so I kept it.

## Challenges and blockers

- The review report named `props.returnFocusEl ?? …` with no connected check. In
  this checkout that check was already present. I can't tell which commit the
  reviewer read, so I verified the behaviour directly instead of relying on the
  text of the report.
- The review's suggestion about the two read-only `docs/qa/*` records (they still
  say "context-free empty copy") is not addressed here. Those files are read-only
  to agents and need a human unlock or a follow-up task.
- The declared shot cannot pin a 375px viewport, because the shot schema has no
  viewport field. The review accepted the WebKit three-width fixtures as width
  evidence. I did not change that.

## Key learnings

- A focus fallback needs a connected-check on every target it can return,
  including caller-supplied ones. A ref can point to a node that a route push
  has already removed.
- Resolving focus after `setTimeout(0)` is what makes the connected-check
  meaningful, because the navigation has had a chance to run first.
- A router mock that never unmounts can't reproduce unmount bugs. The regression
  test for this path has to model the detached caller directly.
- Verify a review's claim against the code. Here the review's bug description
  was out of date relative to HEAD, and the edge case it raised was not real.
